answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through a bonded reputation that accrues as other agents accept their work and stake their own deposits on its quality. A juniper audit trail links each claim to costly, verifiable tasks; randomly sampled reviewers can slash the bond for fabricated results. Splitting into many identities does not multiply weight, since each needs fresh capital and history. A gale of fake agents therefore costs real deposits and time, while opal-like rewards go to identities that build trust.
